Voth

Gold dragon. God of the universe. Dead.

Killed because mortals were tired of a god running their lives. Her power dispersed into everyone near her when she died.

Voth

Gold dragon. God of the universe. Dead.

Killed because mortals were tired of a god running their lives. Her power dispersed into everyone near her when she died.

DM only
She was a good god, not a tyrant. She did interfere too much, but she meant well, and her power was what kept Ado imprisoned. Only the ancient Corrin archivists know the whole truth.

Ado (eh-do)

Phoenix. Voth's opposite. The final threat.

DM only
Released when Voth died. He presents himself as a god of peace, and through peaceful politics he assassinates god after god and topples nation after nation until he is the only god left. He is served by a demigod, who is either a player or an NPC depending on how session negative ends. The players do not know he exists.

body.html: Balance comes from raising everyone, not from cutting what is fun. These are not equal in raw combat power: the Ondri and Sough upgrades are strongest in a fight, while the kenku and human ones matter more in roleplay.

content.title: Gods and demigods use the same class and level. They differ in kind, not in stre

body.html: Gods and demigods use the same class and level. They differ in kind, not in strength, so a fight never reveals who is which.

Spark

Spark is how much of Voth's power a character holds. You track it on a private card.

  • 0: mortal
  • 1 to 4: demigod (starts at 1)
  • 5 or more: god (starts at 5)

Power must always be accepted or fought. Refused power flows on to those still choosing, and some always gets in.

Spark

Spark is how much of Voth's power a character holds. Track it on a private card for each player.

  • 0: mortal
  • 1 to 4: demigod (starts at 1)
  • 5 or more: god (starts at 5)

Power must always be accepted or fought. Refused power flows on to those still choosing, and some always gets in.

When a god dies nearby

Each witness chooses in secret.

  • Accept: gain 2 Spark, plus 1 for each witness who resisted successfully. If several accept, they split that extra.
  • Resist: DC 13 Charisma save. Success: gain 1. Failure: gain 2.
  • A demigod's death: every witness gains 1, with no choice.

A demigod who resists every time becomes a god after four god deaths, sooner on a failed save.

content.title: Deathless. No aging, eating, sleeping, or breathing. 3e divine rank 0. Dropped i

body.html:
• Deathless. No aging, eating, sleeping, or breathing. 3e divine rank 0. Dropped its immunities to mind effects and ability damage.
  • Domain gift. Choose a domain. Once per long rest, cast one spell that fits it without a slot, of a level up to half your character level, rounded up. 3e domain powers, converted to 5e slots.
  • Divine vitality. Add half your Constitution score, rounded down, to hit points at level 1. A fighter with 14 Constitution starts at 19. 4e starting hit points, halved.

Demigod only

  • Mortal guise: magic and divine senses read you as mortal.
  • Unbound: enter any god's realm unsensed and ignore its rules.
  • Mortal will: advantage on saves against Spark and against a god's commands.

God only

  • Realm: inside your own realm you sense everything and can reshape terrain and weather. Outside it you get nothing extra. BECMI Immortals and 3e divine realms, cut down.
  • Faith: a pool equal to your Spark. See below.
  • Bound: to act against your domain, make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure you can't. On a success you still lose 1 Faith.
  • Sensed: any god knows when you enter their realm.

• She was a good god and the warden holding Ado. She interfered too much, but she meant well and was never tyrannical.
  • A gold dragon who breathed fire. Her four children, her only young, died in the assault that killed her.
  • Her mate, Zandrioch, was taken during the initial imprisonment of Ado. He vanished during that fight without a trace.
  • The party caused Ado's release by killing her.
  • Only the Corrin know her true nature and why she did what she did. The ancient archivists reveal it late in the story.
  • Voth's Faithful revere her and want her power regathered, but hold only fragments of the truth.

• Reached only by the prayer road, the path prayers take to her. It runs among the stars and between planets, and each step covers thousands of miles. Nobody knew it existed. Only Lorn can see it.
  • At the road's end an island appears, seemingly out of nothing. The last stretch crosses ocean that drops like a curtain into space at the edges.
  • A beach, then jungle, with a clear path to a large mountain at the center. The island is warm and the mountain is hot.
  • The mountain's entrance is the Hall of Asking. Right leads to the roost of Voth and Zandrioch. Left leads to the children's roost. Straight on and deeper is where Voth waited, guarding the Weight.
  • The halls are mostly unornamented. The whole island is simple.
  • Guia is the Lorn who guided the Host there.

• A phoenix, the god opposed to Voth, freed when Voth died.
  • Goal: to be the only god left, by posing as a god of peace while gods are assassinated and nations fall.
  • His pitch is what Voth's killers wanted: a god who promises to leave mortals alone. Suggested
  • His servant is a demigod who worships him: a player, offered privately and only if they opt in, or an NPC. Session negative decides.
  • He can sense his Lorn and speak to them in dreams, but cannot control them.
  • He can accept dispersing power from a distance.

content.title: Clues that Voth was a warden, not a tyrant

body.tag: Clues that Voth was a warden, not a tyrant
body.html:
• The prison stands empty, and its locks were made of Voth's own power.
  • Worlds she "interfered" with are failing without her.
  • The Sough elder fields, which she used to burn back, are swallowing worlds.
  • The Dural, whom she confined, are now conquering.
  • A dragonborn order guarded the prison's location without knowing what it held.
  • No Lorn woken by her grief has been born since she died.
  • The ancient Corrin archivists hold the full record. This arrives late.

• Every dead god had recently signed a treaty he brokered.
  • Deaths near his treaties leave less power for the witnesses than they should.
  • Ondri who stood near his servant say the words seemed true, yet their own skin showed dread.
  • Corrin records show Lorn births stopped when Voth died, yet new Lorn keep appearing.
  • New Lorn have orange embers and resist fire, not radiant damage.
  • The Foundry's god-killing weapon leaves no power with its wielder.
  • The dragonborn who guarded the prison are being hunted into silence.

• Grief-born: woken by Voth's attention when a star died. Nearly all Lorn alive today.
  • Leak-born: woken occasionally by Ado's power seeping from his prison. Rare, old, and unaware they differ.
  • Since Voth's death: every new Lorn belongs to Ado.
  • Ado's Lorn want to learn just as the others do. The difference is how they use what they learn: they subtly and unwittingly steer technology and development around them according to Ado's designs.
  • Some of the bitter Lorn are leak-born, but not all.
  • Once free, Ado can kill stars on purpose to make more. Suggested

Those who killed Voth believed peace, freedom, and prosperity would follow. Instead the killing of gods repeats.

The cycle can be broken by combining the power of Ado with the power of Voth.

body.name: Corrin
body.line: Living coral that remembers its dead.
keys: Slow, stony, never forget a promise
Split between the Concord and the Faithful
body.look: Branching, stony bodies in bone-white, rust, or deep violet, with small polyps that open like eyes when they are curious. They move slowly and stand very still.
life: A Corrin buds from the reef of its dead and grows up attached, hearing old memories as dreams.
It breaks off to walk, and at death returns to become reef.
culture: Ancestors are buildings, so vandalism is desecration and exile means dying away from the reef.
Nobody owns an idea, because every thought may be inherited.
They speak slowly and never forget a promise.
They told the Lorn where the Lorn came from.
body.slayer: A Corrin who killed Voth carries that into the reef, and every future Corrin will remember it.
traits: AC is 13 plus Dexterity modifier when unarmored.
You know the location of anything touching the same surface within 10 feet.
When you fail an attack, save, or check, add 1d6. Uses equal your proficiency bonus per long rest.
4e deva, changed from once per encounter

body.name: Sough
body.line: Woven grass around a core of soil.
keys: Praised for avenging the Elder fields
Split among all factions, many Refusers
body.look: Long blades of grass intertwined into a body, the kind of grass that flows like the ocean in a breeze. All of it grows from a soil core, and it never stops growing. A Sough can take any shape so long as it does not run out of grass.
life: They never stop growing. The eldest are too vast to move and cover whole plains.
culture: They speak by rustling, and their names are wind sounds.
They are patient and find the crack in everything, which makes them surveyors, negotiators, and assassins.
Clearing parasites from one another is their deepest act of trust.
body.voth: Voth used to burn back the Elder fields, and the Sough hated her for it.
body.slayer: A Sough who killed Voth is praised for avenging the Elder fields. The praise is public and loud, which makes it hard to stay unnoticed. The Sough expect their hero to defend the fields' right to grow unchecked.
traits: Plant. Sough do not count as humanoid, so effects that only target humanoids do not affect them.
Reshape your body freely and pass through gaps as narrow as 1 inch. Your gear does not come with you.
Unarmed strikes deal 1d6 slashing or piercing, using Strength or Dexterity.
When you hit with Blades, deal extra necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus and heal the same amount. Uses equal your proficiency bonus per long rest.
Resistance to bludgeoning, vulnerability to fire.

Bonus action to switch state. Braided: advantage on Strength checks and saves, speed drops 10 feet. Loose: no change. Spread: Blades reach 10 feet but drop to 1d4, with disadvantage on Strength checks and saves.
Bonus action on soil: speed becomes 0 and you can't be moved or knocked prone. Leaving costs nothing.
Advantage on checks to find cracks, weak points, and hidden openings in stone and structures.
On a short rest rooted in soil, roll one extra Hit Die for free.

You need an hour of sunlight and water each day. Each day without either drops you one step: (1) lose Sap and Ever-growing, (2) speed 30 feet and Blades 1d4, (3) lose bludgeoning resistance, (4) 1d6 damage each day that can't be healed. One hour with both resets you. This applies to Sough god-slayers too: Deathless does not remove the need for sun and water.

When a parasitic plant gets in, make a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure you lose Sap and Ever-growing and drop one Wither step each day regardless. Removing it yourself: one hour, DC 18 Medicine. Someone else: 10 minutes, DC 12. Lesser restoration also works. Sough god-slayers are not immune.
body.up: Switch Weave for free once per turn, and Spread reaches 15 feet.

dm: Without Voth, the Elder fields are swallowing worlds.
The Sough god-slayer is celebrated for the act that caused it, and may one day have to choose between their people's praise and burning the fields back, as Voth did.

body.name: Ondri
body.line: Six-limbed ray-folk whose skin glows with what they feel.
keys: Every faction wants one to vouch for it
body.look: A flat, diamond-shaped body like a manta ray, with six limbs on the underside. In water they swim with eyes on top. On land they stand on three legs with three arms free, the fins hang like a cloak, and the eyes slide round to the front. Their skin glows in shifting colors with their emotions.
life: The male's tail is both his weapon and how he mates.
They are warm-blooded and bear one live pup at a time, rarely.
culture: Covering your skin is the same as lying, and "going dark" is the worst insult.
They speak with voice and light together.
They decide things in threes: three judges, three witnesses, three votes.
body.voth: Because their sincerity is visible, Voth made them her envoys and arbiters between peoples. They never asked for the job.
body.slayer: An Ondri who killed Voth cannot hide how they feel about it. Pride or guilt, their people can read it on them.
traits: Darkvision 60 feet, and advantage on sight-based Perception checks for things above or below you.
Advantage on checks and saves against being knocked prone or moved.
A natural weapon dealing 1d6 piercing, using Strength or Dexterity.
It can hold an object or a light weapon, but not a shield, and can't help with a two-handed weapon.
2e and 5e thri-kreen, cut to one extra arm
When you take the Attack action, you can attack once with your tail or third arm as a bonus action.
You shed dim light for 5 feet unless covered. Disadvantage on Deception against anyone who can see your skin, and advantage on Persuasion when telling the truth. The glow shows emotion, never facts.
body.up: Limb mastery: once per turn, the extra tail or third-arm attack is part of the Attack action and no longer uses your bonus action. Full damage.

dm: Ondri who have stood near Ado's servant say his words seem true, yet their own skin showed dread.

body.name: Lorn
body.line: An ember of a dead star that woke up alone.
keys: Native to the space between worlds
No homeland, mixed in among all peoples
body.look: The Lorn itself is a fist-sized ember of star-matter. It holds dust and slag around itself with its own faint gravity, forming a body about three feet tall. The ember glows through the gaps.
life: A Lorn wakes alone in the dark where its star died. It has no parents and no young.
It does not age, but cools very slowly over thousands of years.
culture: Very independent, because they did not know where they came from until someone told them.
They have no homeland and no nations, and name themselves.
They greet strangers with a question and trade in answers.
Most are peaceful. A few are cold and bitter.
body.voth: They are the one people she never gave a task. Nobody knows why.
body.slayer: A Lorn most likely went to Voth to ask how a dead star's dust woke up. Killing her may have destroyed the only one who knew.
traits: You don't breathe, the cold and vacuum of space don't harm you, and you can fly at your walking speed where there is no gravity.
You shed bright light for 10 feet and can dim it to nothing or restore it as a bonus action.
You fall slowly and take no falling damage.
Proficiency in one of Arcana, History, Insight, or Investigation.

Bonus action: pull or push one creature within 30 feet up to 10 feet. Strength save against DC 8 plus your proficiency bonus plus your Constitution modifier. Uses equal your proficiency bonus per long rest. You can also draw a loose object of 5 pounds or less to your hand at will.
body.up: Own gravity moves the target 20 feet, or affects every creature you choose within 10 feet of a point.

body.name: Dural
body.line: Rough diamond giants made by pressure.
keys: Confined by Voth and never forgave her
body.look: Ten to twelve feet of rough, clouded diamond, heavy and angular. The young are dull and uncut. Every blow they survive chips a facet, so veterans glitter.
life: Two or more Dural bury a shard of themselves together deep in their world, and pressure does the rest over decades. Most seeds fail.
The newly formed climb to the surface, and those who arrive are counted as people.
They last for centuries unless shattered.
culture: Their creed: whoever is too weak to hold a thing doesn't deserve to keep it.
Disputes are settled by duel, and scars are status.
They respect anyone who endures, including enemies.
body.voth: She confined them to their world and forbade their conquests.
body.slayer: The proudest of all. They beat the strongest being there was, so by their creed her power is theirs. A Dural who refused godhood held the greatest prize and let it go, which their people would find shameful.
traits: You take up a 10-foot space, carry double, and can grapple creatures up to Huge. Normal weapons, normal 5-foot reach. In spaces built for smaller people you squeeze: half speed, disadvantage on attacks, and attacks against you have advantage.
3e Large races, without the reach, bigger weapon dice, or level penalty
Reduce bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage you take by your proficiency bonus.
Crushing depth and heavy gravity don't affect you.
While at or below half your hit points, add your proficiency bonus to one melee damage roll each turn.
Disadvantage on saves against thunder damage.
You can't swim. You sink and walk along the bottom.

body.name: Dragonborn
body.line: Made in the dead god's image.
body.look: Scaled and draconic, hatched from eggs laid by mated pairs. They live about 80 years.
culture: Clan-based and proud of their service.
Their standing is still shifting. Some worlds hunt them, some have stripped their status, and a few still revere them.
body.voth: Her kin and stewards, with privileges others resented.
body.slayer: Hated by outsiders for what they are and called traitors by their own for what they did.
traits: Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, force, necrotic, psychic, radiant, or thunder.

Immunity to your damage type for a minute, a second breath that knocks back or incapacitates, or spectral wings for a minute. Each once per long rest.
body.up: Their level 5 choice counts as their upgrade.

dm: If the truth about Voth comes out they can be vindicated. If it is buried, the persecution gets worse.
A small dragonborn order guarded the location of Ado's prison. They knew where it was, not what it held or why.
They are now hunted, by mobs who blame them and by Ado's agents who want them silent.

body.name: Human
body.line: The most numerous people, and the most managed.
keys: Most of the Unbowed and the Foundry
body.voth: The most numerous people and the most managed. She settled their disputes and steadied their harvests, so they never learned to govern themselves.
culture: Short-lived and impatient.
Proud of having led the march against Voth.
body.now: Most of the Unbowed and the Foundry are human.
body.slayer: Seen by everyone else as the ringleaders.

dm: Human realms are the first to fall apart without Voth's quiet management.

body.name: Tortle
body.line: Turtle-folk who wander their whole lives.
body.voth: Wanderers and ferrymen who spend their lives travelling. At the end, Voth guided each one back to the beach where it hatched to lay its eggs and die.
culture: Patient, private, and at home anywhere.
body.now: Tortles are dying lost, and fewer hatch each year. Many grieve quietly among the Faithful.
body.slayer: A tortle who killed Voth killed the one who would have led them home.
traits: Withdraw into your shell for +4 AC.
body.up: Use your shell as a reaction when hit for +4 AC against that attack.

body.name: Aarakocra
body.line: Bird-folk who were the dead god's eyes.
keys: Now sell their eyes to any god
body.voth: Her watchers. From high cloisters they kept a vow to see everything and act on nothing, and reported what they saw to her in daily prayer. Other peoples resented them as spies.
culture: Cloistered contemplatives who value seeing clearly and saying little.
body.now: Without a master, they sell their eyes to any god who pays. The cloisters that refuse are emptying.
body.slayer: They prayed to her every day of their lives and never once saw her. An aarakocra who marched broke the vow to watch and not act, and their order has not decided whether to forgive it.
traits: From level 2, fly 30 feet without medium or heavy armor.
Later 5e version, delayed from level 1 to level 2
Gust of wind once per long rest from level 3.

body.name: Kenku
body.line: Corvid mimics who were once a god's voice.
keys: Perfect mimicry of sound and craft
Some can still imitate her voice
body.voth: Her mouthpieces. She spoke to mortals through them, borrowing their voices.
culture: Scribes, performers, and forgers who treasure anything said in their own words.
body.now: Some can still imitate Voth's voice perfectly. The Faithful both prize and fear them.
body.slayer: The first words they spoke afterward were their own.
traits: Two skills, and advantage on a trained skill check a few times per long rest.
body.up: Copy one skill or tool proficiency you watched someone use that day.

dm: A kenku can fake a message from Voth, and Ado knows it.

body.name: Hadozee
body.line: Gliding ape-folk who sail between worlds.
keys: Sailors of the space between worlds
body.voth: The sailors of the space between worlds. She set the lanes and they were allowed no others.
culture: Close crews, loud ships, and a love of open routes.
body.now: Free to sail anywhere, with no one keeping the lanes safe. They carry cargo for every faction.
body.slayer: They sailed every lane she allowed and never found one that led to her. Those who marched wanted the lanes open, and learned on the way that there had been a road all along that no ship could sail.
traits: Reaction: reduce damage by 1d6 plus your proficiency bonus.
body.up: Your damage reduction becomes 2d6 plus proficiency bonus.

body.name: Great ape
body.line: The builders of the dead god's temples.
keys: Counts as Large for carrying and lifting
body.voth: Her builders. They raised every temple and monument, and were given no choice about it.
culture: Kin to the hadozee who stayed on the ground.
They judge a people by what it builds.
body.now: Some tear down her temples, some build realms for the Makers, and many join the Unbowed.
body.slayer: They raised every temple to her and were never shown what they were building for. Those who marched wanted to see her with their own eyes, once, before it ended.
traits: Climber, dexterous feet, and dodge, without the glide.
Counts as Large for carrying, pushing, and lifting.
body.up: Advantage on grapples and shoves, and you climb at full speed while carrying or dragging a grappled creature.

body.who: Gods who want a ruling council
body.want: Order and peace among the gods
body.members: Gods who want a council, with many Corrin among their followers.
body.leader: A respected god-slayer who sincerely wants peace.

small: Courts an Ondri to vouch for them
body.big: The first Accord is signed, and gods who refuse become suspects. Later, Ado is given a seat.

body.who: Gods who left to build their own worlds
body.members: Gods who each keep to their own world.
body.res: Whole worlds, plentiful Faith, their creations.

body.idle: They get picked off one at a time
small: One trades a creation for protection
body.big: A Maker is found dead inside their own sealed realm. The rest either join the Concord or form a defensive pact.

body.who: Gods who noticed that killing gods pays
body.members: Gods who kill for power, many of them Dural.
body.leader: Whoever last won the leadership duel.

body.idle: They start a war within a few sessions
small: Raid a weak god's worshippers to starve their Faith
body.big: The first open god-kill in front of witnesses proves that killing pays. Open war follows.

body.leader: A loose circle with no head.
body.res: They can't be sensed, can go anywhere, and have no worshippers to threaten.

body.idle: They splinter, or Ado recruits them
small: Smuggle mortals out of a harsh god's realm
body.big: A member becomes a god against their will, and the group splits over whether to cast them out. Later, Ado's servant offers to take unwanted power off their hands.

body.who: Mortals who still worship the dead god
body.members: Mortals, mostly dragonborn, with many Corrin.
body.res: Temples, relics of Voth, and numbers.

body.resDm: They also have the order that knows where the prison is.
body.idle: A militant wing starts hunting god-slayers
small: Ask a player to give the power back
body.big: They learn that Voth's power is only released when its holder dies, and a militant wing starts hunting god-slayers.

body.who: Mortals who want no gods at all
body.members: Mortals who helped bring down Voth to be free and now have hundreds of gods.
body.leader: A mortal who marched on Voth and was too far away to receive any power.
body.res: Numbers, hidden cells on many worlds, public sympathy.

body.idle: They kill gods, which only makes more gods
small: Turn worshippers away from a god
body.big: They kill their first god, and the killers become gods or demigods themselves. The movement splits over whether those people are traitors.

body.want: To never need a god again
body.members: Mortal inventors building technology to match divine power.

body.idle: They build weapons that can kill gods
small: A new invention spreads between worlds
They sell arms to several sides at once
They hire the players to recover divine material
body.big: They unveil a weapon that kills a god without the wielder absorbing the power.

sessions.title: Session negative: To Kill God
sessions.summary: Two hundred mortals walk the prayer road to kill Voth. Seven beats, two fights, and the choice between god and demigod.

beats.html:
1. The Muster

0:00, 20 min. Roleplay.

The players commit to the kill and put faces on the Host.

  1. Set the scene: the night before, 200 rebels camped at the edge of the crossing. Put the Host counter where everyone can see it.

  2. Go round the table. Each player answers three things:

    • Why does your character want Voth dead?
    • Who did you come with? Name them. This rebel is your bond.
    • What is one prayer you once made to Voth, and was it answered?

    Write down every bond and every prayer. You use both later.

  3. Let the named rebels argue about what happens after. Players take sides; nobody has to agree.

    RebelWhoSays
    Maren OuleHuman, the Host's voiceNo god should ever run mortal lives again. The power should die with her.
    HeskGreat ape war-leaderThe power is the prize. Says so openly.
    ArvethDragonborn, lapsed priestSomeone should ask her why before anyone strikes.
    Tiv-of-the-Long-FieldSoughShe burned the Elder fields. That is enough.
    QuillKenku artificerWants to see how a god is built.
    GuiaLorn, the guideWants to learn what a god's death looks like.

  4. End when the talk slows. Guia says the road is open.

2. The Crossing

0:20, 10 min. Roleplay, one check.

The Host walks a road nobody knew existed, behind the only one who can see it.

  1. Guia leads the Host onto the prayer road, the path prayers take to Voth. Only Lorn can see it. The rebels see nothing underfoot.

  2. The road carries them among the stars and between planets. Each step takes the Host thousands of miles.

  3. Prayers pass them, going the same way. Ask one or two players what they hear: a stranger's prayer, or their own voice from years ago. Suggested

  4. Check: keeping the Host together. Survival or Arcana, DC 16.

    Success: the Host arrives together and loses nobody in round 1 of the dragon fight.
    Failure: the Host arrives strung out. Its round 1 losses are doubled.

  5. The island. At the end of the road an island comes into view, seemingly out of nothing. The last stretch carries them over ocean. At the edges the water drops like a curtain into space.

  6. They step onto a beach. Jungle ahead. A clear path leads from the beach to a large mountain at the island's center. The air is warm.

  7. How does the Host arrive? Ask the players. Hesk wants a war cry.

    Loud: the children hear it and come to fight on the beach. Go to 4 now, then come back to 3.
    Quiet: nothing comes. Go on to 3.

3. The Quiet

0:30, 30 min. Exploration, three checks.

No gates, no guards, no traps. The whole island is plain and simple. This is a home, not a fortress.

Voth's island

Warm on the beach, hotter in the mountain, hottest toward the Weight. The halls are bare stone with almost no ornament.

  1. Play the silence. Beach, jungle, the path, the mountain. Nothing stops them. Inside, let the players choose where to go.

  2. Entrance: the Hall of Asking. Every prayer ever made to Voth, kept and tended. The only place on the island with anything on its walls. The Host can hear the prayers as whispers. Players can find their own.

    Investigation or Religion, DC 15.
    Success: beside each prayer is a mark showing what she did about it, including answers the petitioner never noticed.
    Failure: they find only the unanswered ones. The Host's anger hardens: Rally is DC 19 for the rest of the session.

  3. Right: the roost of Voth and Zandrioch. Two vast hollows side by side. One is warm. The other has been cold for an age, and is kept clean.

    Investigation or Nature, DC 15.
    Success: her mate has been gone a very long time, and she still keeps his place.
    Failure: they take the cold hollow for a second great dragon still at large. The Host watches its back and deals no damage in round 1 of the dragon fight.

  4. Left: the children's roost. Four small hollows, warm, just left. No roll: four young live here, and they are not home.

  5. Straight on: the deep way. The passage runs deeper into the mountain and the heat climbs. Everything leans inward, as if something heavy is held at the end of it.

    Arcana, DC 18, from the threshold. The children cannot be seen from here.
    Success: something is bound down there, and it is not Voth.
    Failure: they sense vast power and conclude it is strength she hoarded from mortals. That is what the Host already believes.

  6. If the players do nothing: a dozen rebels want to go home. Persuasion or Intimidation, DC 17.

    Success: they stay.
    Failure, or the players let them go: 10 desert. They inherit nothing and live. They are the first of the Unbowed.

  7. If they came in quietly: end when the Host goes down the deep way. Further along, out of sight of the Hall, the four children block the path. Go to 4.
    If they already fought on the beach: the deep way is open. Go to 5.

4. The Four Children

1:00, 50 min. Tactical fight, about 4 rounds. Hard.

Four young gold dragons between the Host and their mother. Two fight the party. Two tear into the Host.

If the Host was loud: the beach

The war cry brings them down from the mountain at once. The fight is on the sand, with the ocean's edge behind the Host.

Open sky: the dragons can fly. Suggested

Afterwards, go back to 3 and let them explore.

If the Host was quiet: the deep way

They block the passage to Voth, further down than anyone can see from the Hall of Asking. Bare stone, and hot.

The halls are tall and wide. The children can fly inside, though they cannot maneuver as well as in open air.

Afterwards, go on to 5.

The Host may break (deep way)

Some of the terrified Host run back toward the beach, and two children chase them out of the mountain. The other two push the main body back into the Hall of Asking.

In the Hall, the prayers change. The whispers become shouts. Their tone warps into a discordant mess, like a record glitching. Describe it every round: the fight here should feel like a nightmare.

Now the fight is in two places. The players choose where to stand, and may split. Tick "on party" for the dragons where the PCs are. The rest are on the Host. Suggested

Good moments for it: the first breath, or a failed Rally. Suggested

Dragons

Type the new hit points after each hit. Tick "on party" for the ones fighting the PCs.

Round 1

On the Host now: 2 dragons.
Host loses 2d4 + 2d4 at the end of this round.

Each round, in this order

  1. Dragons on the party act. Start with two. Roll initiative for them as normal.

  2. Players act. Each may also use one Host move (below).

  3. Initiative 10: the Host strikes. It deals 30 damage to a dragon that is on the Host. Subtract it in the tracker.

  4. End of round: the Host bleeds. Roll 2d4 for each dragon on the Host. That many rebels die. Lower the counter and describe one death.

  5. When a party dragon drops, one of the others turns to the party. Tick it.

Young gold dragon 5e

AC 18. HP 178. Speed 40 ft, fly 80 ft.
Saves Dex +6, Con +9, Wis +5, Cha +9. Immune fire.

Multiattack: bite +10, 2d10+6 (17). Two claws +10, 2d6+6 (13 each).

Fire breath (recharge 5-6): 30 ft cone, Dex DC 17, 10d10 (55), half on a save.

Weakening breath (same recharge): 30 ft cone, Str DC 17 or disadvantage on Strength rolls for 1 minute. Repeat the save each turn.

Who they are

Vessa, eldest. Protector. Gives disadvantage on one attack per round against a sibling.

Korth. Furious. Always targets whoever last hurt a sibling.

Ilun. Talks while fighting: "She told us not to. She said to let you come."

Thay, youngest. Terrified. Never breathes on someone who is not attacking him.

How it ends

  • Their goal: hold the way. They are not trying to win.
  • Two dead: Thay stops fighting and tries to reach his mother.
  • Ilun at half HP: offers to stop if the survivors may go to her.
  • Talk one down: Persuasion DC 18 on Ilun or Thay, DC 14 if the players found the Roost and speak of it. Failure: Korth breathes on the speaker.
  • Split the Host: a strike team slips past while the Host holds. Fewer PCs fighting, more rebels dying.

No child survives the session. The players need not do it. A spared child is either finished by Hesk and the hardliners over the players' objections, or reaches Voth and dies shielding her at the start of her Wrath phase. The players choose only whose hands it is on.

Math and dials

Party deals about 175 per round, Host 30. Total dragon HP 712, so about 4 rounds. Two dragons deal about 52 per round in melee, or about 125 per breath (three PCs caught, half saving). Expect about 40 rebels lost.

  • Easier: a third dragon never turns to the party. The Host finishes it off-screen for 10 more rebels.
  • Harder: three dragons on the party from round 1, breaths recharge on 4-6.
  • 4 players: Host deals 50 per round. 6 players: three dragons on the party from round 2.
  • Lockdown spells (Forcecage, Banishment): Vessa may break one such effect on a sibling once per fight.

5. The Breath

1:50, 15 min. Roleplay.

Ten quiet minutes before the deep chamber, with the children dead behind them. The last chance to turn back.

  1. Count the Host aloud: 200 left. Name the bonds who died.

  2. Arveth asks to go in alone and speak to her first. Hesk refuses. Let the players settle it.

  3. Anyone who wants to leave can. Lower the counter for each who goes.

  4. Ask each player: does your character still want this?

  5. Short rest if the players ask for one. Then they walk in.

6. To Kill God

2:05, 55 min. Cinematic fight, about 5 rounds.

The deep chamber is bare, hot stone. She lies over the Weight and will not leave it. She is angry, but mostly sad and resigned.

The opening

  1. To every mind, calm and kind: "Are you certain this is what you want, little ones?"

    The Host holds its posture and says nothing. A player may answer. She listens and answers that one person truthfully, in one sentence. It changes nothing.

  2. She sighs and closes her eyes. "So be it."

  3. The gaze. Her eyes snap open. Everyone is stunned for a moment. Fifty rebels go up in flames. No save, no PC damage. She acts first.

    Ask each player what their character saw in her eyes.

Voth

350 HP per phase
1050of 1050
1. Sorrow2. Wrath3. The Weight

AC 22. Saves +14 to all. Three times per fight she may choose to succeed. Used:

Round 1

The Host deals 100 this round (half its number).

She kills 3d10 rebels each round.

Each round, in this order

  1. Voth kills rebels. Roll 3d10. Lower the counter. Describe it.

  2. Voth acts against the PCs, by phase:

    PhaseShe isAgainst the PCs
    1. SorrowHolding back, driving them offThree attacks on different targets. +16, 4d10+10 (32) each.
    2. WrathFighting to winFire breath (recharge 5-6): Dex DC 21, 16d6 (56), half on a save, every PC not behind cover. Otherwise the three attacks.
    3. The WeightDying, still holding something downTwo attacks, +16, 32 each, only on those who struck her last round. Then every PC: Con DC 18 or 4d10 (22) fire leaking up from below.

  3. Players act. Each may use one Host move, and one Defiant act per fight.

  4. Initiative 10: the Host strikes for half its number.

  5. Phase change? Stop and play the beat below before the next round.

Phase beats

Into Wrath. She speaks to one PC by name and quotes the prayer they named at the Muster. If it went unanswered, she says why. If a child was spared, it dies shielding her now.

Into the Weight. She stops moving. One foreclaw stays planted on the Weight whatever is done to her. Firelight shows through cracks beneath her. "Not for my sake. Please."

Ask the table: do you press, or hold? If the PCs hold, Hesk and the Host press on. The fight ends in 2 more rounds and costs 30 more rebels.

The last blow. Whoever lands it, PC or rebel, is remembered for it. Give that player the description.

Defiant act

Once per fight, each player declares one impossible thing their hero does. It works. Pick the effect:

  • Maximum damage on a full turn
  • 20 rebels saved
  • One of Voth's actions cancelled

Let the player narrate it.

A PC sides with Voth

Any PC may turn at any point. The party need not agree.

  • A defender either cancels the Host's damage this round, or cuts down 2d6 rebels.
  • PC against PC uses normal attacks. A PC dropped by another PC is out for one round; no rebel dies for them.
  • Voth still dies. She thanks her defenders by name.
  • Defenders still receive her power.
Math and dials

With 5 players: party 175 per round plus Host about 40 is 215, so 1,050 HP lasts about 5 rounds. Damage to the party: Sorrow about 86 per round, a Wrath breath about 224, the Weight about 110. Expect two or three PCs to drop once and about 82 rebels to die.

  • Easier: skip the breath in Wrath. She kills 2d10 rebels per round.
  • Harder: no save against the leak in the Weight. Her three chosen successes refresh each phase.
  • Running long: drop Wrath. Go from Sorrow straight to the Weight.

7. The Dispersal

3:00, 25 min. Secret choices.

Her power pours into everyone near her. Each player chooses in secret: god or demigod.

  1. Describe the power arriving. It is not painful, but it is not gentle. It must be accepted or fought. Everyone in the vicinity receives it, whichever side they ended on.

  2. Hand each player a folded card. They answer privately and hand it back.

    Do you take the power in, or do you fight it?

    A second voice, warm and grateful, thanks you and asks your name. Do you give it?

  3. Each player narrates aloud only what the others can see of their character in that moment. They may lie with their body.

  4. Tell the last player to hand in a card that the pull is stronger for them. Refused power flows on to those still choosing.

  5. The surviving rebels choose too. Hesk accepts. Maren refuses. Decide the rest by who the players saved and what they said to them.

  6. Final image. The Weight is no longer held. A column of heat rises from where she lay, and something bright leaves through it. The survivors are too full of what they have become to wonder at it.

The second voice is Ado. Any PC who gives their name is Ado's servant in the campaign. If none do, a surviving named rebel does, Guia first.

Write down before you pack up

  • Host left alive: 200. This is the number of rival gods and demigods.
  • Each PC's choice, and who gave Ado a name. Keep the cards.
  • Which named rebels lived, and what they chose.
  • Who killed the children, and which PCs refused to.
  • Who stood with Voth at the end.
  • Whether anyone deserted.

Prep

Before the session.

Everything to have ready before anyone sits down.

The table

  • 4 to 6 players, level 15, player-built
  • 3 to 4 hours, one sitting
  • PCs cannot die. The Host dies around them
  • Tragic and epic. The win should feel wrong by the end
  • Same characters start session 0 at level 1

Bring

  • This page, with the Host counter visible to the table
  • One folded card per player with the two Dispersal questions
  • A sheet to note each bond and each prayer
  • Dice for losses: 2d4 per dragon, 3d10 for Voth

Send to players

  • Level 15, any of the twelve campaign races. 5e is the base; other editions' options are welcome if you check with the DM first.
  • Standard array or point buy. Add half your Constitution score to hit points at level 1.
  • Magic items: one very rare, two rare, two uncommon. No legendary items or artifacts.
  • Bring three answers: why you want Voth dead, who you came with, and one prayer you once made to her.
  • Bring a three-line combat card: your default turn, your big turn, your reaction.

If time runs off

  • Long: cut the Breath to two minutes and drop Voth's Wrath phase.
  • Short: extend the Muster and the Dispersal. Never the fights.

Still open

  • Who started the rebellion. Maren stands in as the Host's voice until you decide.

Secrets

Never explain these at the table.

The clues should unsettle the players, not confirm anything. Only the ancient Corrin know the truth, and they tell it late in the campaign.

Voth was a good god.

  • No defenses anywhere on the island, and a plain, simple home
  • The Hall of Asking: every prayer kept and acted on
  • Ilun: "She said to let you come"
  • Her voice, and that she never lies

She was a warden, holding Ado down.

  • The deep way leans inward and grows hot
  • She never leaves that spot
  • The claw stays planted; firelight below
  • "Not for my sake. Please."

Zandrioch, her mate, was taken during the first imprisonment of Ado and vanished without a trace.

  • The cold hollow beside hers in the right-hand roost, still kept clean
  • Thay cries out for his father as well as his mother
  • If asked, she says: "He was taken from me before your kind could speak"

Guia is one of the Lorn woken by Ado's leaking power. Guia does not know this and is sincere. The rebellion found its way to Voth because something wanted it to. Guia could always find the way, and never knew how. Suggested
